characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe-7Al-1.0C shows the highest precipitate density: bright lenticular/needle-shaped and rounded particles in a darker matrix.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: hot-rolled plate; etched; scale bar 250 µm in panel (e)
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal microstructure and precipitate distribution as a function of carbon.

characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe3Al and Fe3AlC0.5 peaks; similar peaks observed in alloys with 0.35–1 wt.% C, confirming Fe3AlC0.5 in Fe-7Al-1.0C.
characterization_methods.purpose: Confirm the precipitate phase Fe3AlC0.5 in the carbon-series alloys.

processing_steps.method: air induction melting with flux cover (AIMFC)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Forty-kilogram melts of the carbon-series alloys were prepared by air induction melting with a flux cover (Al2O3, CaO, MgO, CaF2); melt top poured into split cast iron molds.
Ingots preheated in a hearth furnace at 1373 K for 1 h and hot-forged in a 1-tonne pneumatic forge hammer with die platens at room temperature.
24-mm-thick sections preheated at 1373 K for 1 h, hot rolled 50% with 1-mm reduction in thickness per pass; samples reheated after every six rolling passes; final thickness 12 mm.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: hot-rolled plate (Table V caption labels route 'AIM'; text b0060 states air induction melting with flux cover)

phases_present.morphology: bright lenticular/needle-shaped and rounded particles; highest precipitate density at 1.0 wt.% C

precipitates.distribution: high density of bright lenticular/needle-shaped and rounded particles dispersed in a darker matrix; volume fraction highest at 1.0 wt.% C

structures.overall_structure: Hot-rolled Fe-7Al-1.0C consists of an Fe3Al matrix with a high density of Fe3AlC0.5 precipitates (bright lenticular/needle-shaped and rounded particles in a darker matrix).

unmapped_findings: The volume fraction of Fe3AlC0.5 precipitates increases significantly with increasing carbon content, being highest in Fe-7Al-1.0C (b0061, figure_005).

The room-temperature ductility decrease with increasing carbon is attributed solely to the increase in the volume fraction of hard and brittle Fe3AlC0.5 precipitates; Fe-7Al alloys are not susceptible to environmental embrittlement (b0062).

Table V and Fig. 5 captions for the carbon-series alloys label the melting route 'AIM', while the section text (b0060) states the alloys were prepared by air induction melting with a flux cover (AIMFC).
